stories.headline: BJP wins West Bengal for the first time; Suvendu Adhikari sworn in as first BJP Chief Minister
stories.summary: The BJP swept West Bengal state assembly elections on May 4, winning 207 of 294 seats and ending 15 years of Trinamool Congress rule under Mamata Banerjee, who refused to resign and was later removed when the Governor dissolved the assembly. Home Minister Amit Shah oversaw the selection of Suvendu Adhikari as CM; PM Modi and Shah attended the swearing-in ceremony at Brigade Parade Ground in Kolkata on May 9. The victory prompted extensive commentary on BJP's consolidation of national power, allegations of voter roll manipulation, and opposition calls for unity.

stories.headline: Jaishankar concludes three-nation Caribbean tour, signs eight MoUs with Trinidad and Tobago
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar completed a multi-leg Caribbean tour covering Jamaica, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago between approximately May 2–10. In Trinidad, he inaugurated an agro-processing facility, launched a Jaipur Foot prosthetics centre, signed eight MoUs covering tourism, healthcare, infrastructure and Ayurveda, visited Nelson Island with PM Kamla Persad-Bissessar, and engaged the Indian diaspora. In Suriname he co-chaired the 9th India-Suriname Joint Commission Meeting. The tour aimed at deepening India's strategic and cultural engagement with the Caribbean.

stories.headline: Operation Sindoor one-year anniversary: India commemorates, Pakistan issues warnings, both sides claim victory
stories.summary: India marked the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor — the May 2025 four-day military conflict with Pakistan — with official commemorations, a Joint Commanders' Conference, and a new documentary. PM Modi changed his social media profile to the operation's logo. Pakistan's military issued warnings against any attack and unveiled new missile systems, while both governments held press conferences claiming strategic success. Al Jazeera and AP News covered the anniversary as a moment of continuing tension.

stories.headline: Modi appeals for fuel conservation, gold abstinence, and WFH as Iran war drives energy crisis
stories.summary: Speaking at a development event in Hyderabad on May 10, PM Modi publicly urged citizens to conserve fuel, avoid foreign travel and non-essential gold purchases for one year, and revive work-from-home practices, citing disruptions to global supply chains caused by the US-Iran war and the resulting pressure on India's foreign exchange reserves. Congress attacked the appeal as 'clueless' and 'reckless'; Home Minister Amit Shah and Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri backed Modi's call.

stories.headline: India appoints new CDS and Navy Chief amid push to finalize integrated theatre commands
stories.summary: The government appointed Lieutenant General NS Raja Subramani (retd.) as the next Chief of Defence Staff and Vice Admiral Krishna Swaminathan as the new Chief of Naval Staff, effective when incumbent CDS General Anil Chauhan's extended tenure ends on May 30. Raja Subramani, who previously served as military adviser at NSA Doval's National Security Council Secretariat, will oversee the long-delayed formation of three integrated theatre commands. Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan was simultaneously named to lead the Western Naval Command.

stories.headline: Indian military outlines Vision 2047 and integrated theatre command reforms post-Sindoor
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and the Indian Armed Forces released a Vision 2047 roadmap and a Joint Doctrine for Integrated Communication Architecture at the second Joint Commanders' Conference in Jaipur. The conference drew lessons from Operation Sindoor and ongoing global conflicts, outlining goals for space-based ISR, cyber defence, indigenous procurement, and the creation of three integrated theatre commands. Analysts noted the new CDS appointment directly enables this reform agenda.

stories.headline: Amit Shah chairs high-level review on flood and heatwave preparedness, orders Flood Crisis Management Teams in all states
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a comprehensive high-level meeting in New Delhi on May 10, reviewing India's preparedness for the upcoming monsoon season, potential floods, and heatwaves. Shah directed that Flood Crisis Management Teams be constituted in every state, ordered early warning systems for 60 high-risk glacial and mountain lakes across Himalayan states, and called for integrated flood forecasting. The meeting was framed around PM Modi's 'zero casualty disaster management' vision.

stories.headline: Amit Shah speaks on democracy, AI and judiciary at Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's book launch
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah attended the launch of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's two books at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on May 10, also attended by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Attorney General Venkataramani. Shah praised India's 76-year democratic resilience, argued that the strength of democracy lies in institutional balance rather than confrontation, and warned that AI and modern technology may pose fresh challenges to the judiciary. The event coincided with Mother's Day, prompting personal remarks from Shah about his late mother.
